title: Small Models, Big Results: Training a Finance Agent for Under $500 — Charles Dickens, Snorkel AI
talk_summary: Snorkel trained a 4B Qwen model with RL on expert-validated financial QA/tool-use data for under $500, and it beat its 235B variant on a held-out FinQA benchmark. The transferable mechanisms are leakage-controlled domain evals, layered data verification, simple binary rewards, and fixing tool-use discipline before reasoning depth.

takeaways.what_they_do: They build expert-validated FinQA from real 10-K tables and split by company so benchmark companies never appear in train/val.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the data is split so that no company in the benchmark overlaps um in any split

takeaways.what_they_do: They verify generated QA with programmatic consistency checks using lineage/table metadata, independent agent reviews, then expert manual review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: three-layer verification process... programmatic consistency checks... automated reviews from independent agents... expert manual review
takeaways.numbers: ~6,900 tables generated; ~7,000 tables in training environment

takeaways.technique: Small specialist via RL for narrow subtasks
takeaways.what_they_do: They fine-tune a 4B Qwen model with GRPO and binary reward on domain tool-use tasks, beating a much larger variant at a fraction of cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we got a 4 billion parameter model to outsmart its 235 billion parameter variant

takeaways.what_they_do: They identify schema hallucination, context flooding via SELECT *, and poor error recovery as core failures; training simple single-table tool use generalized to multi-table tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The bottleneck was never reasoning depth, it was just tool use
takeaways.numbers: Simple-data training gave the most lift and generalized to multi-table without explicit multi-table training

takeaways.technique: Evaluate environment, horizon, and output complexity
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue agent evals must cover realistic environment complexity, autonomy horizon, and output complexity, not just text artifacts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: environment complexity is um, one of the most important axes

takeaways.what_they_do: They ran roughly 1,000 concurrent environments to generate trajectories and found a single binary correctness reward beat a more engineered rubric.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A single binary reward signal, um, was what got us the most lift
